headline.headline: BREWERS ONE WIN FROM PENNANT AS BAUERS, MITCHELL BLAST DODGERS INTO CRISIS
headline.deck: Back-to-back homers off Snell in seventh send Milwaukee to 3-0 series lead
headline.body:
LOS ANGELES — Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back home runs off Blake Snell in the seventh inning Wednesday night, turning a tight pitchers' duel into a rout and lifting the Milwaukee Brewers to a 6-2 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers at Dodger Stadium before 50,708 stunned fans. Milwaukee now leads the National League Championship Series three games to none and can complete a sweep in Game 4 Thursday night.

The Brewers had scratched out a 1-0 lead in the first inning and neither club scored again until the Dodgers tied the game and briefly took the lead with two runs in the sixth. Milwaukee answered immediately and decisively. Bauers connected first against Snell, Mitchell followed him out of the park moments later, and by the time the seventh inning was finished the Brewers had scored three times to take a 4-2 lead they would not relinquish, adding insurance runs in the eighth and ninth.

Ryan Wrobleski earned the victory, and Dodgers starter Shohei Ohtani was hit by a pitch from Milwaukee reliever Bryan Gasser in a night that went wrong early for Los Angeles and never recovered. The Brewers, who went 103-59 during the regular season to win the NL Central, are three outs from their first World Series appearance in decades. The Dodgers, the NL's second-best team at 100-62, face elimination Thursday in their own ballpark.

secondary.headline: FOX, HARPER, CASTLE TRIPLE THREAT ARRIVES AS SPURS ROLL SUNS
secondary.deck: San Antonio's three-guard lineup debuts with force in 123-103 playoff win
secondary.body:
SAN ANTONIO — The experiment is over. The reality has arrived. San Antonio Spurs coach Mitch Johnson finally deployed his three-guard lineup of De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle together Wednesday night, and the result was a 123-103 demolition of the Phoenix Suns in the second round of the NBA playoffs. The Spurs' speed and ball movement overwhelmed a Suns defense that had no credible answer for the trio.

The victory extended San Antonio's playoff momentum and set the tone for what promises to be a compelling second-round matchup. Fox directed traffic with veteran poise, while Harper and Castle applied relentless pressure off the ball. Phoenix, which finished the regular season at 103 points in the loss, was simply outmanned at every guard position on the floor. The series now shifts in San Antonio's favor.

secondary.headline: CROSBY SCORES TWICE AS PENGUINS HEAD TO DENVER TO FACE AVALANCHE
secondary.deck: Pittsburgh captain's two-goal night sets the stage for a marquee Western matchup
secondary.body:
PITTSBURGH — Sidney Crosby delivered another reminder of his enduring brilliance, scoring two goals in Pittsburgh's most recent outing to send the Penguins into Wednesday's road date against the Colorado Avalanche with momentum at their backs. Pittsburgh enters at 3-3-1 on the young NHL season while Colorado sits at 4-2-1 in the Central Division, making the matchup one of the more compelling early-season tilts on the schedule.

Crosby's two-goal performance underscored why Pittsburgh remains a legitimate threat despite questions about the team's depth. Colorado, playing at altitude at Ball Arena, presents a stiff test. The Avalanche have won four of their first seven and will look to their own veteran core to neutralize the Penguins captain when the puck drops Thursday night in Denver.

secondary.headline: SEAHAWKS BANGED UP HEADING INTO THURSDAY NIGHT VISIT TO DENVER
secondary.deck: Seattle rules out linebacker Thomas and running back Charbonnet for Broncos game
secondary.body:
SEATTLE — The Seattle Seahawks will travel to Denver for Thursday night's game without two key contributors after the team officially ruled out starting linebacker Drake Thomas and running back Zach Charbonnet. Thomas's absence leaves a significant hole in Seattle's defensive front seven, while losing Charbonnet reduces the Seahawks' options in a backfield that was already operating under scrutiny.

The Broncos, playing at home in Denver, figure to benefit from the personnel losses. Meanwhile in New Orleans, Saints quarterback Tyler Shough and head coach Kellen Moore addressed criticism from owner Gayle Benson publicly on Wednesday, with Shough acknowledging he shares the owner's frustrations over the team's recent struggles. The comments drew attention across the league as the Saints attempt to stabilize a turbulent situation midseason.

column.headline: THE DODGERS ARE NOT DEAD YET, BUT SOMEBODY SHOULD TELL THEIR BULLPEN
column.body:
Three games in and the Los Angeles Dodgers, baseball's glamour franchise and the team everyone expected to waltz into November, are one loss from watching Milwaukee hoist the pennant on their home field. The Brewers have not beaten the Dodgers so much as they have exposed them. Snell surrendering back-to-back home runs to Bauers and Mitchell in the seventh inning of a tied game is not a fluke. It is a pattern, and Los Angeles has no answer for it.

Milwaukee won 103 games during the regular season and nobody outside of Wisconsin seemed to take that seriously enough. They should have. The Brewers play clean, patient baseball, and they do not rattle. Dodger Stadium was packed with 50,708 believers Wednesday night and it did not matter one bit. Game 4 is Thursday, and the smart money says the Brewers will not leave California empty-handed. Sometimes the best team in baseball is not the most famous one.

story.headline: BREWERS BASH DODGERS TO BRINK OF ELIMINATION, LEAD NLCS 3-0
story.deck: Back-to-back homers by Bauers and Mitchell in seventh seal 6-2 Milwaukee victory
story.body:
LOS ANGELES — The Milwaukee Brewers are three wins from the World Series and the Los Angeles Dodgers are three losses from going home. Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back home runs off Blake Snell in the seventh inning Tuesday night at Dodger Stadium, turning a 2-1 deficit into a 4-2 lead and powering Milwaukee to a 6-2 victory that pushed the Brewers' NLCS advantage to three games to none.

The Brewers had scratched out a first-inning run and then watched the Dodgers answer with two runs of their own in the sixth to seize a 2-1 edge. But the seventh inning unraveled Los Angeles entirely. Bauers launched his first homer of the postseason, Mitchell followed with his own shot — his first as well — and Jackson Chourio, who had gone deep earlier in the series with his second home run of these playoffs, capped a three-run frame that broke the game open. Milwaukee added single runs in the eighth and ninth to complete the rout. Starter Colin Wrobleski earned the win.

With 50,708 fans sitting in stunned silence, the Dodgers managed to reach base repeatedly but could not convert, stranding 19 runners on the night while Milwaukee left 10. Shohei Ohtani was hit by a pitch from Bryan Gasser and continued what observers have called an inexplicable postseason slump. No team in major league history has recovered from a 3-0 series deficit to win a League Championship Series, and Game 4 is scheduled for Thursday in Los Angeles.

story.headline: HEAT TORCH NETS IN SEASON OPENER, 144-128
story.deck: Miami erupts for 144 points as Brooklyn's defense offers little resistance in Tuesday blowout.
story.body:
MIAMI -- The Miami Heat wasted no time announcing their intentions for the 2026-27 NBA season, dismantling the Brooklyn Nets 144-128 Tuesday night at Kaseya Center in a performance that was never seriously in doubt. Miami's offense operated at a relentless pace throughout, piling up points against a Brooklyn defense that could find no answers, turning what might have been a competitive season opener into a convincing statement.

The San Antonio Spurs also impressed in Tuesday's action, rolling past the Phoenix Suns 123-103 at home in a game that offered a glimpse of what new Spurs coach Mitch Johnson has been building. Johnson debuted a three-guard lineup featuring De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle, a bold alignment that tormented Phoenix and gave San Antonio a decisive edge in ball movement and perimeter scoring. The Suns, unable to contain the trio, fell by 20 in a result that raises early questions about Phoenix's defensive roster construction.

In the night's tightest contest, the New Orleans Pelicans edged the Dallas Mavericks 101-97 at American Airlines Center, handing Dallas a narrow and painful home-opening loss. The Pelicans held on down the stretch to escape with four points, giving New Orleans a road victory that will loom large in the early Western Conference standings. The Boston Celtics also cruised, beating Charlotte 114-93 to serve notice that last season's championship hunger remains very much intact.

story.headline: TUCH POWERS CAPITALS PAST CANADIENS IN 5-4 THRILLER
story.deck: Washington forward tallies twice and adds assist to fuel dramatic win over Montreal
story.body:
Alex Tuch was everywhere Wednesday night, scoring twice and adding an assist to lead the Washington Capitals to a 5-4 victory over the Montreal Canadiens. Tuch's three-point performance gave Washington the edge in a back-and-forth contest that saw the lead change hands multiple times across regulation.

In Denver, the Dallas Stars needed four rounds of a shootout before Roope Hintz delivered the decisive shot, sending the Stars past the Colorado Avalanche 3-2. The teams played through a regulation tie before heading to overtime and eventually a shootout, with Hintz finally ending the marathon night in the fourth round to claim the extra point for Dallas.

Looking ahead, the Avalanche face a quick turnaround Thursday when Sidney Crosby and the Pittsburgh Penguins visit Ball Arena. Crosby is riding a two-goal performance and will test a Colorado squad now sitting at 4-2-1 in the Central Division. Boston, meanwhile, carries a three-game winning streak into Anaheim against the Ducks, with the Bruins posting a 5-2 mark in the Atlantic Division.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS RETOOL FOR 2026
story.deck: Several franchises are reshaping their rosters around new signal-callers this spring.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has turned into a full-blown quarterback market, with teams across the league scrambling to secure their franchise signal-callers before training camps open in late July. The Las Vegas Raiders, still searching for stability under center after a turbulent 2025 campaign, reached an agreement with veteran quarterback Sam Darnold on a two-year deal worth $58 million, betting that a change of scenery can unlock the arm talent that briefly dazzled scouts in Minnesota. Meanwhile, the Cleveland Browns, fresh off another disappointing finish, have made contact with the representatives of free agent Geno Smith, whose market has proven surprisingly robust for a player entering his age-36 season.

The NFL Draft, held in late April in Washington D.C., reshuffled the league's balance of power in significant ways. The New Orleans Saints, picking second overall, selected Colorado quarterback Shedeur Sanders, ending months of speculation and giving the franchise its most high-profile signal-caller since Drew Brees. The Tennessee Titans used the first overall pick on Miami edge rusher Nic Scourton, addressing a pass rush that ranked among the worst in the league last season. Draft analysts at NFL Network praised the Titans' haul, calling Scourton the most NFL-ready defender in the class.

On the trade front, the Dallas Cowboys sent veteran wide receiver CeeDee Lamb to the Detroit Lions in a blockbuster deal that sent three draft picks back to Dallas, a move that signals a full rebuilding effort in Texas under first-year head coach Mike Zimmer. Lions quarterback Jared Goff, coming off a strong 2025 season, now has one of the most dangerous receiving corps in the NFC. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones addressed the trade at a press conference Tuesday, insisting the organization remains committed to competing while acknowledging that the front office is prioritizing long-term flexibility heading into the new league year.
